name: MFCR
full_name: MFCR: magnetic-controlled flexible continuum robot with C, J and S deformation modes, steered by a three-dimensional electromagnet platform
group: Tsinghua University, State Key Laboratory of Tribology in Advanced Equipment (Zili Wang, Ding Weng, Zhaoxin Li, Lei Chen, Yuan Ma, Jiadao Wang) (wang2023_magnetic p. 1)
target_anatomy: coronary access through aorta-coronary bifurcations (PTCA-type guidewire navigation, Sec. 3.2); tested in 3D-printed ring channels (ID 4 mm, 30-130 deg), simplified aorta-left/right coronary models at three angles, and a Y-bifurcation with clay obstacles (Sec. 3.2-3.3, Figs. 5-6)
devices_driven: its own magnetic soft continuum robot (guidewire-like): silicone elastomer with NdFeB powder (1:1 by mass) as the magnetic tip, nitinol-core silicone body (Sec. 2.2); advanced into the branch 'with the help of manual operation' (Sec. 3.2)
n_dof_detail: tip deformation set by the field direction and strength (three planar modes C, J, S); insertion by hand (Sec. 3)
translation_detail: magnetic (steering); forward push by hand ('with the help of manual operation', Sec. 3.2)
rotation_detail: magnetic torque of the external field on the programmed magnetisation; no axial rotation (Sec. 2.1, 3.1)
device_range: magnetic part L = 15 mm (segments 6, 3 and 6 mm with different magnetisation), D = 1.5 mm (Sec. 3.1, Fig. 3)
imaging_compat: optical: DSLR camera, camera above the testbed (Fig. 1c, Sec. 3.1); fluoroscopy N.R.
validation_detail: bench: static deformation in the three-dimensional electromagnet platform against the model, n = 3 per condition (Sec. 3.1, Fig. 4); phantom: passing 30-130 deg ring channels and aorta-coronary models with a permanent magnet (Fig. 5), and entering a branch past an obstacle with J and S modes in the electromagnet system (Fig. 6, Videos S1-S2)
key_numbers: C-shape field 19.7-127 mT; < 150 mT in all tests (Sec. 4); max mean angle error 2.979 deg and max mean tip-position error 0.328 mm (Sec. 5); J mode 0.589 / 0.499 deg and 0.103 mm (Sec. 4); magnetised at 1.5 T for 10 s (Sec. 2.2)
sim_model: yes: quasi-static model from magnetic plus elastic potential energy on an Euler-Bernoulli beam, solved in MATLAB to predict the deformation modes (wang2023_magnetic Sec. 2.1, 3.1)
